questions.question: Which statement best defines the purpose of Architecture Diagram Builder?
options: An architecture diagram makes system boundaries, responsibilities, request paths, data stores, and external dependencies visible enough to review before implementation.
It is only a visual dashboard with no decision model.
It is a storage engine that replaces every system dependency.
It guarantees a production design without workload evidence.
questions.explanation: An architecture diagram makes system boundaries, responsibilities, request paths, data stores, and external dependencies visible enough to review before implementation. The tool structures this decision; it does not remove the need to validate assumptions.

questions.question: What information should be established before relying on Architecture Diagram Builder?
options: Only the name of a preferred vendor.
Place only components with distinct responsibilities, then connect the user-facing path and asynchronous work separately.
questions.explanation: Place only components with distinct responsibilities, then connect the user-facing path and asynchronous work separately. Explicit inputs keep the result tied to a reviewable workload rather than a generic recommendation.

questions.question: How should the output of Architecture Diagram Builder be interpreted?
options: Treat it as proof that no failure can occur.
Ignore the assumptions once a result appears.
Check that every arrow has a direction and purpose, every stateful component has an owner, and failures cannot silently cross boundaries.
Choose the largest result without reviewing trade-offs.
questions.explanation: Check that every arrow has a direction and purpose, every stateful component has an owner, and failures cannot silently cross boundaries. The result is evidence for a design review, not an automatic production guarantee.

questions.question: Which experiment best tests whether the current Architecture Diagram Builder result is robust?
options: Keep every input at its default value.
Skip the failure and boundary cases.
Remove one dependency or mark it unavailable, then trace which user actions survive and which require degradation.
questions.explanation: Remove one dependency or mark it unavailable, then trace which user actions survive and which require degradation. Changing a consequential assumption exposes where the current design stops being safe.
